stories.Headline: Law Society issues practice note tying solicitors' AI use to existing duties and insurance checks
stories.Summary:
The Law Society published a new practice note on 21 October 2026 that brings together existing professional obligations and practical guidance on using AI in legal practice. It follows the SRA's strongly worded warning notice in August, which Hogan Lovells Cadwalader examined at the time. The note distinguishes AI used in the "practice of law", such as legal research, drafting and analysis, from AI used in the "business of law", such as billing and marketing. It states that there is no AI-specific regulator for the legal sector, so solicitors' use of AI sits within existing professional, data protection and cybersecurity frameworks, including the SRA Standards and Regulations. The note also addresses insurance, highlighting the potential implications of firms' use of AI for both professional indemnity and cyber insurance.

The note says the SRA has not certified AI products and that responsibility for work produced using AI remains with the solicitor and cannot be transferred to the technology provider. It states that AI cannot reliably verify its own output, so lawyers should check AI-generated material against authoritative sources rather than asking the same, or another, AI system to confirm it. It cites Ayinde v London Borough of Haringey and Al-Haroun v Qatar National Bank [2025] EWHC 1383 (Admin), in which the High Court addressed the use of false authorities and emphasised lawyers' responsibility for material put before the court. It cites SRA v Kumar, in which a Registered Foreign Lawyer was removed from the Register of Foreign Lawyers after repeatedly relying on false or unsupported AI-generated authorities, including following an express warning. It cites R v FGD [2026] EWCA Crim 918, in which the Court of Appeal warned that using AI to prepare a witness for cross-examination may amount to coaching and, in an extreme case, create sufficient unfairness for the court to consider excluding evidence.

The note states that although there is currently no general obligation to disclose the use of AI, transparency may be appropriate where AI has been used materially in preparing documents. It states that a witness statement must remain the witness's own evidence and accurately reflect their recollection. It cites the Civil Justice Council's final recommendations on AI use in court documents, published on 29 October 2026, which propose that factual witnesses should declare that AI has not generated or influenced the substantive content of their statements, with a different disclosure requirement for expert evidence. It cites R (Munir) v Secretary of State for the Home Department [2026] UKUT 81 (IAC), in which the tribunal highlighted the potential confidentiality and privilege consequences of uploading client material to a publicly available AI tool. It states that using an "enterprise" or specialist "legal AI" product does not remove these risks, and that information described as anonymised will only fall outside data protection law where individuals are genuinely no longer identifiable.

The note states that AI may create new categories of potentially relevant material, including prompts, draft outputs and audit logs, whose treatment under existing privilege principles remains largely untested. It states that a business user may ask AI for legal advice and create unprivileged material, even if it is later sent to the legal team. It states that professional competence increasingly includes understanding the systems lawyers use and their limitations, and that one particular concern is automation bias, where users place undue confidence in an output simply because it has been produced by technology. It states that professional liability could eventually arise from failing to use AI where a reasonably competent lawyer would have done so, and that there is currently no positive professional duty to use AI, but the applicable standard of care may evolve as increasingly reliable tools become embedded in legal practice.

It states that the risks become more significant with AI agents and agentic AI, which can take actions and carry out multi-step processes across systems with reduced human intervention. The note states that firms should limit systems' permissions to what is genuinely necessary and build in appropriate human review and approval points as autonomy increases. It states that firms need effective AI governance even if they have not formally adopted AI, because staff may independently use publicly available tools, creating the risk of "shadow AI". It states that appropriate controls may include an AI-use policy, approved-tools list, restrictions on the information that may be entered into AI systems, staff training and clear processes for escalating errors or data breaches.

It states that clients should receive appropriate information about how AI may be used on their matters, which firms can address upfront through engagement letters or terms of business. It states that where work is billed by time, firms should not charge for the hours the task would have taken without AI, and that any separate AI or technology charge should be transparent, agreed appropriately and should not duplicate other fees. The note states that AI risks extend beyond hallucination and confidentiality, and include bias and discrimination, cybersecurity, operational resilience and concentration risk arising from dependence on particular technology providers. On professional indemnity insurance, it recommends that firms consider whether their use of AI changes their professional indemnity risk profile or falls outside the considerations upon which their insurance was arranged.

It recommends that firms check whether their existing professional indemnity policy, proposal form or renewal documentation asks about matters such as the use of AI, automation and legal technology. It recommends that firms consider their disclosure obligations including in respect of risks that the firm ought to be aware of, in addition to those which the firm is aware of. It recommends that firms maintain clear supervisory documentation and evidence of risk management, as insurers may be interested in the firm's AI governance processes and may ask about the extent of human oversight of AI-assisted work. More to follow.

stories.Headline: Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia head amid scandals and federal investigations
stories.Summary:
Jensen Huang resigned as the head of Nvidia last Thursday after admitting to an extramarital affair with Alice Huang. This Singapore based executive is believed to be a spy for China, which created a major scandal for the company. A New York Times report also stated that the chief executive had a second affair with a subordinate at Nvidia. These revelations led to federal investigations and a sell off of the company stock by many worried investors.

The scandal involves the easing of export controls on AI chips that were originally established under the administration of Joe Biden. Jensen Huang lobbied President Donald Trump to allow more chip sales to China, which he argued would maintain a United States advantage. The Commerce Department reportedly stopped an investigation into whether Alice Huang smuggled chips into China after an Nvidia lawyer contacted them. Trump was warned about the relationship with the suspected Chinese asset last year and again in May before a Beijing trip.

President Donald Trump said on Monday that he hoped there was no problem regarding the situation with the former chief executive. He has continued to describe Jensen Huang as an honorable, amazing, and high quality guy who will end up in good shape. Stephen Witt told the New Yorker that it is generally regarded as bad if a chief executive is sleeping with spies. The president previously decided that AI companies should self police after meeting with Huang and other executives in the tech industry.

The AI company Anthropic is preparing an initial public offering estimated at 1.4 trillion dollars and has received investment from Nvidia. Anthropic has warned its potential investors that artificial intelligence technology poses existential or catastrophic risks to the future of all humanity. The current board of Nvidia is populated by longtime associates and early investors who had no succession plan for the company. This lack of planning means that the company was left without a clear replacement when the chief executive finally resigned.

Nvidia was the most powerful and valuable AI company in the world and Huang served as the closest adviser to the president. The company is now being led by chief financial officer Colette Kress while the search for a permanent replacement begins. The current administration has followed a laissez faire approach to AI regulation that was pushed by the former chief executive. This approach is now being questioned as the technology is seen as dangerous and ill understood by many outside observers.

The new Congress includes members who were elected on promises to rein in data centers and other aspects of AI technology. These members may find it challenging to change current policies as long as Donald Trump remains in power in Washington. The articles leave open whether the federal investigations will lead to criminal charges for the former chief executive or others. It remains unclear if the United States will reinstate the stricter chip export controls that were previously eased by the president.

stories.Headline: Carlson LLC sues Anthropic and Meta for using self-help books to train AI models
stories.Summary:
Carlson LLC filed a federal lawsuit on November 19, 2026, against the artificial intelligence companies Anthropic PBC and Meta Platforms, Inc. The plaintiff claims that these two tech giants illegally used more than two dozen self-improvement books to train their AI models. These literary works were written by the husband and wife team of R. and K. Carlson, including the famous Don't Sweat the Small Stuff series. The legal action was brought in the Northern District of California under case number 3:26-cv-14248. The complaint alleges that the defendants harvested training materials from pirate libraries such as Anna's Archive and Books3. It further asserts that the companies scanned physical books without permission to feed their respective systems, Claude and Meta AI.

Carlson LLC specifically opted out of the Bartz class action settlement with Anthropic to pursue this separate claim. The company argues that these bestsellers are more valuable than other works and have suffered direct harm from competition with large language models. Brian Matthew Grossman of Tesser Grossman LLP is representing Carlson LLC in this copyright infringement matter. The plaintiff maintains that the books in question possess a long and successful history that distinguishes them from other literary works. While the lawsuit joins both Anthropic and Meta in one complaint, it does not identify a coordinated copying operation between the two.

The defendants have not yet challenged this joinder, and the court has not yet addressed the issue. This case follows other attempts to sue multiple AI companies together, which judges Pitts and Chhabria previously rejected in other lawsuits. Those judges ruled that alleging multiple defendants infringed the same copyright does not satisfy the legal requirements for joining parties. It remains to be seen if the court will allow Carlson LLC to distinguish its case from those prior rulings. The legal process will determine if the AI companies are liable for using the copyrighted self-help materials.

stories.Headline: Jay Clayton says patching PHP security gaps causes some systems to fail
stories.Summary:
Multiple tech outages occurred across various sectors during the week ending November 19, 2026, affecting banking, travel, and government services. These disruptions were caused by routine updates, security patches, or other malfunctions at several major companies and government agencies. Microsoft, Apple, and JPMorgan Chase experienced failures, while the Federal Aviation Administration and National Security Agency also faced issues. The Trump administration stated there was zero indication that these separate events were linked or caused by cybercriminals. These incidents have raised fears that such widespread technological disruptions could become the new normal in an interconnected world.

Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, failed late last week due to a latent defect in a summer network fix. On Friday, a Federal Aviation Administration network malfunction caused the longest nationwide ground stop in 25 years, lasting over four hours. United Airlines faced its own system outage on Monday, while JPMorgan Chase reported a software bug affecting internal hardware systems. On Tuesday, Apple Music, the App Store, and AppleCare failed, and Marriott reported technical issues with website and app sign-ins. The National Security Agency reported that a classified communications network went offline Tuesday during scheduled routine maintenance.

Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton told Fox News that patching security gaps caused some systems to not come back up. He specifically pointed to the patching following a PHP alert from last month as the cause of the NSA outage. Microsoft maintained that its specific outage did not span from AI agents, though it did not specify the network fix goal. Other affected companies, including United, Marriott, and JPMorgan Chase, provided no additional comments to the Associated Press on Wednesday. These organizations and the government all maintained there is no evidence that the disruptions were related to a cyberattack.

Content creator Jake Smith said these concurrent disruptions make people realize how much they rely on systems they do not understand. He noted that seeing several failures happen so close together gives many people a sense of helplessness regarding their digital lives. Social media platforms were filled with a mixture of jokes, confusion, annoyance, and conspiracy theories about the string of outages. Democratic Senator Mark Warner stated these events should be a wake-up call because AI is moving faster than management abilities. Warner also argued that the Trump administration has not shown enough interest in confronting these specific technological challenges.

AI recently helped detect sweeping vulnerabilities for PHP, a general-purpose scripting language that powers websites around the world. Cybersecurity startup Calif used AI to find a software bug in Java, leading Oracle to release a security update. Google reported that cyber criminals are using large language models and agentic frameworks to reverse engineer security patches for vulnerabilities. Professor Justin Cappos noted that AI is better at exploiting bugs than it is at creating patches to fix them. Raj Rajarajan stated that current digital infrastructure was not originally designed to handle the computational demands of large-scale AI.

U.S. cyber authorities issued an advisory on Wednesday urging organizations to install the security update for the Java programming language. Senator Mark Warner suggested that these disruptions are likely the unintended consequences of efforts to make digital systems safer. Experts continue to evaluate the heightened risks posed by AI alongside its ability to detect critical security gaps. The articles leave open whether the Trump administration will increase its efforts to manage the consequences of rapid AI adoption. It remains unclear if the frequency of these outages will increase as AI adoption accelerates across global digital infrastructure.

stories.Headline: Scaling AI Agents Takes a New Operating Model, Not New Tech
stories.Summary:
Antonio Maio discussed scaling artificial intelligence agents during a video interview with ISMG on November 19, 2026. This conversation took place at the Microsoft Ignite 2026 event. Maio serves as a managing director at the firm Protiviti. He explained that moving from pilots to enterprise operations requires more than technology. The process demands a trusted operating model to ensure these agents are secure.

This new model must align identity, data, resilience, governance, and security across the entire organization. Maio highlighted the role of Microsoft's Agent 365 as a control plane for observability and governance. This tool manages agents from the initial ideation phase through to their final decommissioning. He suggested building multidisciplinary pods of experts to support specific client initiatives. Managed services are also recommended as the estates of these agents continue to grow.

Antonio Maio stated that organizations must reshape their operating models to bring siloed business functions together. He noted that agents will touch security, identity, business resiliency, and data in various ways. These areas are often considered separate parts of a business, which complicates how firms govern risk. Maio believes agents will take on greater decision making responsibilities as they embed in processes. He emphasized that a trusted model is necessary to turn experiments into trusted operations.

The agents affect how organizations govern access and decision making because they work across different functions. This cross functional nature creates complications for those responsible for managing risk and security. The articles mention that many organizations have already piloted these artificial intelligence agents in their systems. These entities now face the challenge of scaling these experiments into trusted, enterprise wide operations. The transition impacts how different business silos interact with new agentic AI technologies.

Maio brings more than 25 years of experience in cybersecurity practices and enterprise application architecture. His professional background includes team leadership and information security across both public and private sectors. He has worked with corporate clients in numerous countries and telecom providers in Europe and North America. Additionally, his experience includes working with various military and defense organizations on a global scale. This extensive history informs his views on the governance of next generation AI technologies.

The next steps involve implementing control planes and multidisciplinary pods to manage the growth of AI agents. Organizations must now focus on breaking down silos to integrate security, identity, and data governance. The articles leave open how specific industries will implement these new operating models in practice. They do not detail the exact timeline for when most companies will adopt these changes. There is no mention of the specific costs associated with shifting to this model.

stories.Headline: Anthropic begins trading on Nasdaq at $111.50 per share after filing for IPO
stories.Summary:
Anthropic, the maker of Claude, began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker symbol ANT on Nov. 19, 2026, opening at $111.50 per share. The company filed a Form S-1 with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission ahead of the listing. North Texas investors are poised to benefit from one of the biggest IPOs in history, according to the Dallas Business Journal. The Dallas Business Journal reported on Nov. 18, 2026, that Dallas-Fort Worth investors stand to gain from the offering. The Business Journals preview said readers could find out who has invested and why as Anthropic looks to go public.

Anthropic earned $33.24 billion in revenue in the first nine months of 2026, according to its IPO filing with the SEC. About 79% of that revenue came from usage fees paid by developers and businesses, and 21% came from subscriptions. Marketplace sales made up about 44% of revenue during the first nine months of 2026. Claude Pro costs $20 a month when billed monthly, and Claude's Enterprise plan combines seat fees with usage billed separately at API rates. Anthropic has said it won't put ads in Claude, while OpenAI has been testing Sponsored Agents that let users chat with a business-sponsored assistant after clicking an ad.

Anthropic reported a $1.26 billion operating loss over the same nine-month period, driven largely by high computing costs. Operating expenses totaled $34.5 billion during the nine months, leaving that $1.26 billion operating loss under generally accepted accounting principles. Anthropic reported $4.08 billion in adjusted operating profit after leaving out $3.26 billion in pay through shares or options and $2.09 billion tied to matching employees' charitable donations with company shares. Anthropic says the exclusions make ongoing results easier to compare, and these costs don't involve cash payments, though issuing shares can reduce existing investors' ownership. Anthropic reported a $104.04 billion net loss, about $94.32 billion of which came from earlier financing deals, mainly loans that can turn into shares.

The company recorded $18.81 billion in computing and infrastructure expenses, more than half its revenue, including developing models and running them for customers. Anthropic has committed roughly $900.9 billion to future payments, nearly all for computing and infrastructure, with about $70.7 billion due in the 12 months ending Sept. 30, 2027. Chipmakers such as Nvidia sell the processors used to train and run AI models and get paid when customers buy hardware, whether or not those customers ever turn a profit. Micron, SK hynix and Samsung sell specialized high-bandwidth memory, and Micron pointed to AI-driven demand as it reported a roughly 256% rise in revenue to $133.19 billion for its 2026 fiscal year. Cloud providers such as Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft rent out computing capacity to AI developers like Anthropic and OpenAI and can earn fees when customers buy AI model usage through their marketplaces.

An application programming interface lets a business connect its software to an AI model, and an online store can use a model to answer shoppers' questions and pay for the work done behind the scenes. Text-based API bills often count tokens, and a model charging $2 per million tokens received and $10 per million tokens sent would cost a store $12 for 1 million tokens each way. Amazon Bedrock offers models from multiple AI developers, and Amazon collects the payment and passes the AI developer its share. Generating AI answers takes substantial computing power, and each prompt makes the model perform many calculations to write its answer piece by piece in a process called inference. More efficient chips and models can make AI cheaper to use and encourage more use, a rebound effect that can raise total computing demand, a result known as Jevons paradox.

AI companies often sign long-term contracts to secure computing power, and these contracts typically require minimum payments that remain due even when the company is losing money. Companies sometimes present an adjusted profit that leaves certain expenses out, which can turn a reported loss into a profit on paper without changing what happened in the business. For marketplace sales, Anthropic counts the full customer payment as revenue, and the cloud partner's share appears separately as a sales and marketing expense. The Dallas Business Journal article was previewed at one minute and invited readers to learn who has invested and why as Anthropic looks to go public. The Dallas Business Journal and Regions Bank plan a 2027 Economic Outlook event with an expert look at global, national and regional trends shaping the economy.

stories.Headline: Wenge AI adds Google and Apple sign-in options for international ScienceOra users
stories.Summary:
Wenge AI announced a new update for its ScienceOra platform on November 20, 2026. The company added Google and Apple sign-in options for users of its international site. This change happened in Shenzhen, China, to help researchers access the platform. The update streamlines the registration and sign-in process for overseas scientific researchers. It provides a faster and more convenient way to enter the AI for Science platform.

Users can now authenticate using existing Google or Apple accounts instead of lengthy forms. Apple sign-in is currently available on the web version of the ScienceOra platform. The system identifies whether to create new accounts or sign in based on email status. It improves how third-party accounts link and provides clearer prompts for the Hide My Email feature. These changes aim to reduce duplicate registrations and resolve common sign-in friction for users.

Wenge AI is an enterprise AI company that develops proprietary foundation models and platforms. The company was founded by a team of AI scientists from the Chinese Academy of Sciences. They stated that the refinements maintain a consistent account experience for their international users. The firm intends to continue refining the product experience based on the needs of researchers. They aim to make scientific exploration and access to research tools more seamless.

Overseas researchers are affected by these changes to the AI-powered scientific research and decision-support platform. ScienceOra uses the ScienceOne Scientific Foundation Model to bring together data, tools, and specialized research agents. Meanwhile, the Korean Fair Trade Commission is requiring overseas platforms to appoint legal representatives by January 21. This rule affects companies like Apple, Google, Alibaba, and OpenAI to resolve consumer disputes. The FTC official said that failing to comply will lead to immediate investigations.

The FTC rule applies to businesses with global annual sales of at least 1 trillion won. It also covers platforms with at least 1 million average monthly Korean users during a specific period. Another criterion includes businesses that caused significant consumer harm after violating local e-commerce laws. The FTC met with Alibaba, Temu, and OpenAI on October 28 to review industry feedback. These guidelines clarify the obligations for overseas businesses under the Act on the Consumer Protection in Electronic Commerce.

The FTC will operate a three-month grace period after the system takes effect in January. This period helps companies adjust but does not delay the January 21 appointment deadline. The domestic representative will serve as a formal communication channel for legal notices and investigations. The regulator plans to monitor the implementation of this system and consider further improvements. The articles leave open how many companies will successfully appoint representatives before the deadline.

stories.Headline: NTT DATA and Microsoft partner to build AI-native industry solutions for enterprises
stories.Summary:
On November 18, 2026, NTT DATA deepened its strategic collaboration with Microsoft to build a new generation of AI-native industry solutions for enterprises. Simultaneously, VeriSilicon announced a low-power, high-performance wearable subsystem solution designed specifically for next-generation augmented reality and artificial intelligence glasses in Shanghai. These two separate initiatives aim to advance how artificial intelligence is integrated into both large-scale business processes and wearable consumer hardware. Both companies released these announcements on the same day to highlight their latest technological advancements in the field of artificial intelligence. The efforts focus on moving beyond simple experimentation toward scaled business transformation and efficient computing for advanced wearable device applications.

The NTT DATA and Microsoft effort requires deep industry expertise, scaled forward-deployed engineering capabilities, and frontier technology platforms to succeed. It initially focuses on telecommunications, media, healthcare, life sciences, manufacturing, automotive, and insurance, utilizing the AI Vista platform and 400 reusable assets. NTT DATA plans to mobilize over 500 Microsoft Frontier engineers globally to work directly with clients and domain specialists. VeriSilicon's solution uses FLEXA subsystem architecture and DECNano compression technology to optimize memory bandwidth, data transfer, and overall computing efficiency. This wearable system integrates the Nano-XR series, including ISPNanoUltra-XR, ISPPico-XR, DCNanoUltra-XR, and GCNanoOptimaV-XR, to handle various processing tasks for glasses.

Edwina Fitzmaurice, Corporate Vice President of Industry Solutions Delivery at Microsoft, stated that combining their resources helps clients reimagine how work gets done. She noted that merging Microsoft's cloud and AI platform with NTT DATA's global engineering scale delivers meaningful business outcomes for their clients. The companies believe that technology alone cannot redesign industry processes without people who understand business workflows, data, and regulatory environments. They argue that AI-native solutions should be designed from the start to solve specific problems rather than adding AI to existing workflows. The goal is to identify where artificial intelligence can fundamentally change how industry-specific work is performed to create new value.

Clients in the insurance sector may be affected by reimagining underwriting and claims processes around decisions that are assisted by artificial intelligence. Manufacturing clients could use real-time operational data and AI to identify quality issues and determine the most appropriate response. Healthcare providers might orchestrate complex workflows while keeping clinicians in the loop, and telecommunications firms could improve network and customer operations. VeriSilicon's technology affects the wearable market by providing smartphone-level photo and video quality with optimized power consumption and silicon area. Their ISPPico-XR specifically supports always-on functions for users, such as gesture recognition and eye tracking, within augmented reality glasses.

NTT DATA and Microsoft have a relationship spanning more than 25 years, supported by 23 advanced specializations and six Microsoft Solutions Partner designations. The company holds more than 24,700 Microsoft certifications and currently has approximately 120,000 Microsoft Copilot users globally, including many users in Japan. They use Microsoft AI internally for marketing, IT service management, and employee productivity to gain firsthand experience in driving AI adoption. VeriSilicon built its new wearable solution on a broad portfolio of low-power processing IPs and previous experience in the wearable market. Their existing IP portfolio includes Neural Network, Video, Digital Signal, Image Signal, and Display Processing Units with various configurable options.

NTT DATA will now apply its codified agent patterns, architecture, and connectors to help clients prepare their IT environments for transformative technologies. They will continue to monitor performance and measure business value while determining where human judgment must remain in the loop. VeriSilicon will offer its comprehensive portfolio of processing IPs to address different power and performance requirements for various glasses applications. The articles leave open how these AI-native solutions will specifically perform across different global geographies and diverse regulatory environments. It remains unclear how VeriSilicon's new subsystem will be integrated into specific consumer hardware brands or the final retail pricing.

stories.Headline: Azerbaijan security official warns AI vulnerabilities expose critical infrastructure to faster automated attacks
stories.Summary:
Singapore cyber defenders faced hundreds of AI agents during a national exercise on November 19, 2026, to test their defensive capabilities. These simulated AI agents were capable of taking control of a computer network within hours to challenge the city's security teams. The Critical Infrastructure Defence Exercise used AI tools to help defenders prepare for attacks on transport, water, and power essential services. A fully autonomous AI defence team was also trialled to see if machines could contain attacks without any human intervention. Noah Kong reported on these events which focused on the evolving nature of cyber threats to the nation's critical infrastructure.

The exercise in Singapore occurred while Davud Rustamov spoke in Baku, Azerbaijan, at the 2nd International Conference on Cyber Diplomacy. Rustamov noted that Azerbaijan began establishing a legislative framework for critical infrastructure in 2020, using experience from Italy and the US. Other countries that influenced this framework include Israel and Türkiye, and the legislative process for critical information infrastructure is now complete. The State Security Service of Azerbaijan is the primary authority for security and exercises state oversight over critical information infrastructure. This agency also combats global cyber threats and conducts penetration testing, security audits, and digital forensic investigations for the state.

Davud Rustamov, the Head of the Cybersecurity Operations Center of the State Security Service, spoke during a panel discussion in Baku. He stated that most AI applications contain vulnerabilities because they use a diverse range of software libraries, including some that are outdated. Rustamov explained that these vulnerabilities allow cyberattacks to leverage other AI solutions, and that state affiliated actors specifically target critical infrastructure. He mentioned that the State Security Service shares Indicators of Compromise with international partners and operators of critical infrastructure to strengthen capabilities. Rustamov emphasized that national security agencies must continuously monitor how artificial intelligence is reshaping the current global threat landscape.

Rustamov noted that AI allows existing attack tactics, such as impersonation and reconnaissance, to be executed more rapidly and on larger scales. He stated that operators of critical infrastructure, intelligence services, and national cyber centers must collaborate and exchange information on observed threats. The Azerbaijani official warned that uncensored AI models on darknet resources offer malicious actors extensive capabilities to automate complex attack scenarios. He remarked that law enforcement agencies may not always be prepared to counter these sophisticated attacks using only traditional investigation methods. These threats affect government institutions and the continuous operation of essential services that must be ensured during a cyber incident.

Azerbaijan uses a platform called MISP, where government agencies, private sector representatives, and infrastructure operators share malicious indicators of compromise daily. The country has also joined international MISP Threat Sharing platforms to exchange data on malicious software and threats with local partners. The 2nd International Conference on Cyber Diplomacy was jointly organized by the National Institute for Research and Development in Informatics. Other organizers included the State Service for Special Communications and Information Security, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and the State Security Service. The Office of the President and the Ministry of Digital Development and Transport also participated in organizing the Baku event.

Future priorities for Azerbaijan include elevating international cooperation to an operational level to identify the initial signs of cyberattack campaigns early. Rustamov called for reliable, 24/7 communication channels among national incident response teams and agreements for the rapid exchange of threat intelligence. He suggested that countries should conduct joint exercises to test how coordination will be executed during actual cross border cyber incidents. A proposed unified national cybersecurity landscape would integrate data from law enforcement, intelligence services, and sector regulators onto a single platform. The articles leave open how Singapore's autonomous AI trial performed and the specific results of the Critical Infrastructure Defence Exercise.

stories.Headline: Soket AI raises $4 million from Bajaj Finserv and Pennant Technologies to scale foundation model research
stories.Summary:
Soket AI, an Indian artificial intelligence startup founded in 2019 by Abhishek Upperwal, raised $4 million (around ₹37 crore) in funding, according to TechGig on November 19, 2026. Bajaj Finance invested approximately $2 million in the startup through Bajaj Finserv's applied research and innovation initiative Finserv Intelligence. Pennant Technologies, an investee company of Bajaj Finance, invested another $2 million in the same round. Inc42 reported the $4 million raise on November 18, 2026, from Finserv Intelligence and Pennant Technologies. TechGig reported on November 20, 2026, that Bengaluru-based Soket AI, an IndiaAI Mission startup and frontier AI research lab, secured nearly $4 million from Bajaj Finance and Pennant Technologies.

The funding will support scaling Soket AI's foundation model research and developing AI systems for financial services, cybersecurity, defence and enterprise technology. It will also support applied AI research and enterprise deployments across those same sectors. The startup is building a sovereign open-source AI stack that supports various Indian languages. Soket AI recently launched EKA-1, a 26-billion-parameter foundation model, under Project EKA, its flagship sovereign AI initiative backed by the government's IndiaAI Mission. The startup is working on indigenous foundation models focused on mathematics, coding and reasoning, and its models are designed to run on an organisation's own infrastructure.

Rajeev Jain, Vice Chairman and MD of Bajaj Finance, said the company looks forward to enabling India's indigenous AI ecosystem with Soket AI. He said Bajaj Finance looks forward to engaging with frontier research at an early stage. He said the company will bring its scale and domain expertise to turn this research into practical solutions. The strategic investment is expected to facilitate applied AI research and enterprise deployments across financial services, cybersecurity, defence and enterprise technology. It aims to combine Bajaj Finance's industry expertise with Soket AI's foundational research capabilities and seeks to open opportunities for applied AI research and capability building.

Bajaj Finance aims for secure, cost-effective AI models within its own infrastructure, according to TechGig. Speaking to Inc42 earlier this year, founder Abhishek Upperwal said the idea is to crack the AI model for India first. Soket is among a limited set of Indian AI startups developing indigenous foundation models with support from the IndiaAI Mission. Earlier this month, ZenteiQ AiTech Innovations launched Dhīr 2B and Dhīr 5B, two open-source multilingual models supporting English and 10 Indian languages. Unlike Soket's reasoning-focused EKA-1, ZenteiQ's models are designed as lightweight AI assistants that can run on-premises and on edge devices, including smartphones, without requiring continuous cloud connectivity.

AI unicorn Sarvam AI has expanded its model portfolio with the launch of Prism, an open-weight decision model built on its Sarvam 105B model. The model is designed for enterprise workflows such as customer support routing, security checks and evaluating AI agent activity. Soket AI's EKA-1 model supports 22 Indian languages, code generation and reasoning. The funding comes as the startup looks to scale its foundation model research and develop AI systems for sectors such as financial services, cybersecurity, defence and enterprise technology. Besides financial backing, the strategic investment is expected to open opportunities for applied AI research enterprise applications and capability building.

The articles do not state when the investment closed or the valuation at which the round was raised. They do not name other investors in the round beyond Bajaj Finance, Finserv Intelligence and Pennant Technologies. They do not say how Soket AI will spend the money beyond research, deployments and AI system development. They do not give a timeline for EKA-1's rollout or for the enterprise deployments the funding is meant to support. They do not say whether further funding rounds are planned or how the on-premise models will be priced or distributed.

stories.Headline: ServiceNow survey finds 92% of Indian organisations faced AI agent security incidents in the past year
stories.Summary:
Attackers now have powerful AI on their side, and AI agents can scan, plan and run intrusions at machine speed, improving every month. The result is more attacks, more often and at global scale, so more companies will face a security incident at some point. What separates them is how they respond, and machine-speed threats call for a modern playbook with 4 pillars. The article shows the trend through 6 months of incidents and looks at a few companies, with Fireworks AI as a model of mature, structurally sound response. Several AI platforms disclosed security incidents between May and November 2026.

The playbook has 4 pillars: detect and contain automatically, communicate fast and securely over out-of-band channels, eradicate thoroughly with outside forensic experts, and keep shrinking the blast radius. In November, Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant said AI misuse had reached a "critical inflection point", reporting that attackers use AI to shorten timelines and run multi-stage intrusions at machine speed. CrowdStrike reported that 1 group used AI agents against more than 200 organizations in 11 days, and Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 found attacks moving about 4 times faster than a year earlier. In 2025, Anthropic disrupted a campaign where AI did 80 to 90% of tactical work with little human input. On May 10 and 11, the "Mini Shai-Hulud" campaign altered about 170 npm packages and some PyPI libraries, affecting AI SDKs from Mistral AI and Guardrails AI, and the NHS cyber alert lists the specific versions to avoid.

Klue, a market intelligence platform, disclosed misuse of OAuth tokens it held for customers. Microsoft described intrusions into exposed, unpatched LiteLLM, RAGFlow and Kestra deployments, fixed versions exist for all 3 tools, and CISA had listed the LiteLLM flaw as known exploited on June 8. Anthropic's September threat report described attempts to obtain AI keys through software vendors, and in 1 case instructions were injected into a vendor's automated evaluation sandbox. At least 9 AI developer and hosting platforms disclosed incidents involving stored customer secrets in October, Wiz's tracker later listed further disclosures for 16 platforms in total, and a tampered LiteLLM release, version 1.107.0, was identified with users told to roll back. On November 16, an attacker abused a flaw in Optimizely's account signup flow to inject code into customer projects, reaching 178 organizations' websites according to Report URI, including HSBC, Salesforce, the BBC and Ledger, and the code swapped crypto wallet addresses and skimmed payment forms.

Optimizely removed the payload and fixed the flaw, and Hudson Rock traced similar code through three other web services, beginning November 13. A survey of 500 security leaders by ServiceNow showed that 92 per cent of Indian organisations had an AI agent security incident in the past year, but only 36 per cent of them were able to contain it within 24 hours. Half of the Indian security leaders surveyed described their agentic security as established, but the findings showed uneven foundations, according to the report "Deployed but Ungoverned: The State of Agentic Security in India". Only 19 per cent have a single named individual accountable for agentic AI security governance and 18 per cent have unified, single-interface visibility into their agents. Only 30 per cent enforce an automated deployment gate that blocks agents until they pass security checks, while 47 per cent can produce a complete evidence package on demand.

Kulmeet Bawa, GVP and Managing Director for India and SAARC at ServiceNow, said India's AI ambitions must be matched by the ability to understand, monitor and govern the agents enterprises deploy. He said knowing what an agent can reach is not the same as seeing what it is doing, and automated controls and continuous oversight will be essential to keeping AI innovation underpinned by trust and cyber resilience. He pointed out that AI agents are now part of how Indian enterprises operate, but security has not kept pace. He noted that every agent should be registered, owned and visible in one place, with controls enforced automatically and responses at machine speed, so that security teams can detect problems and contain them in time. About half of the organisations, 51 per cent, have automated real-time detection for anomalous AI agent behaviour, but 67 per cent cannot automatically act when an agent behaves anomalously.

As many as 37 per cent of organisations discovered AI agents running in production in the last 12 months that were never registered or known to security teams. AI has changed the economics of attacking, and tasks that took skilled people days can now be delegated to agents. The tools keep improving, so the pace will keep rising, and AI infrastructure is an especially attractive target because AI access itself has value. The shift started earlier, and incidents appeared across every layer of the AI stack, together showing how broad the activity has become. The last 6 months show what that looks like.

The articles leave open what happens next beyond the pillars and the calls for registration, ownership and automated controls. They do not say whether the 4 pillars were adopted by any named company or what results followed. They do not give the outcome of the Optimizely incident beyond the payload removal and fix, or say how the Hudson Rock tracing through three other web services ended. They do not state what ServiceNow recommends beyond Bawa's remarks, or whether Indian organisations plan changes after the survey. They give no date for when the pace of AI-powered attacks might change.

stories.Headline: Anthropic prices shares at $83 as protesters rally outside Nasdaq
stories.Summary:
Anthropic held its initial public offering at Nasdaq in New York City’s Times Square on Thursday, Nov. 19, 2026, pricing shares at $83. CEO Dario Amodei and his team of executives were at Nasdaq for the opening bell and applauded the listing. Demonstrators gathered outside Nasdaq in Times Square on the same day to raise concerns about AI. The demonstrators held signs reading “Stop Tech Oligarchs” and “Freeze AI” as the stock ticker raced by on screens behind them. Representatives of the group used a small, hot-pink megaphone to address the media and onlookers.

The IPO priced shares at $83, and initial demand appeared strong before the stock started trading at midday. Demonstrators chanted “Hey, hey. Ho-ho. This IPO has got to go!” and “Anthropic, get off it, put people over profit!”

The demonstrators were affiliated with groups including Stop Funding Billionaires, Climate Defiance, Sunrise NYC, Act Up NYC, NYC-DSA, JVP-NYC, Climate Defenders, Planet Over Profit and New York Communities for Change. Their concerns ranged from the potential economic impact if the AI bubble bursts to AI’s effects on the environment, healthcare, surveillance, and jobs. One demonstrator in a Greenpeace T-shirt was led away by police after seating themselves with a sign at the entrance to Nasdaq. James Inniss, an organizer with New York Communities for Change, said Anthropic poses a threat “pension fund-style” because AI is a bubble worse than 2008 with the real estate crisis. Inniss said that if pension funds are stripped in five or 10 years when the bubble bursts, people have to be out there to fight and say that is not acceptable.

Bryce Rogers, an organizer with Resisting Automated Disempowerment (RAD), said he was there to protest that the IPO was moving ahead despite a lack of information about the risks the company’s technology poses. Rogers said he had read auditing firm METR’s recent report on Anthropic but was left with more questions than answers. Rogers praised New York’s Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act and called for more organizing to demand greater regulation and transparency. ACT UP New York’s Brandon Cuicchi said he was concerned about AI’s impact on healthcare, saying hospitals are cutting staff and trying to replace it with AI. Cuicchi said medical offices are trying to pre-screen people with AI instead of a live professional, and that AI is deciding medical outcomes and treatments in the country.

Kenny Moll, an activist affiliated with a campaign called QuitGPT and the Sunrise Movement, said he was concerned about the environmental impact of AI and about the relationship between AI firms, surveillance, and the government. Aber Kawas, a Palestinian-American democratic socialist recently elected as a New York State Senator, said AI companies are among the biggest enemies of the progressive movement. In a statement following the demonstration, organizers attributed a quote to one of the demonstrators who was arrested: “Our demand is clear: freeze reckless AI development and don’t bail out Big Tech when their bubble inevitably pops.” Sifted sat down with Menlo Ventures’ Deedy Das on the sidelines of Slush ahead of Anthropic’s big IPO. Das is a partner at Menlo Ventures, which was an early investor in Anthropic.

Sifted’s interview with Das was published on Nov. 19, 2026, the same day as the IPO. The interview was published under the headline asking whether AI is in a bubble. The articles state that Anthropic’s IPO priced shares at $83 and that demonstrators gathered outside Nasdaq in Times Square on Nov. 19, 2026. The stock was set to start trading at midday on Nov. 19, 2026.

Organizers demanded that reckless AI development be frozen and that Big Tech not be bailed out when their bubble inevitably pops. The articles leave open what Das said in the Sifted interview beyond the headline and the fact that it concerned Anthropic’s IPO and Europe. The articles leave open how the stock traded after it started trading at midday. The articles leave open what happened to the demonstrator who was led away by police.

China's Lenovo reported a forty eight per cent increase in second quarter revenue on November 19, 2026, due to strong artificial intelligence sales. The company earned US$30.2 billion, which exceeded the LSEG consensus estimate of US$27.6 billion based on six analysts. This growth was driven primarily by hardware and servers, with AI related revenue climbing seventy nine per cent to US$10.8 billion. These AI sales now represent thirty six per cent of the total revenue for the group.

The Infrastructure Solutions Group achieved its strongest quarter ever as revenue for data centre equipment rose one hundred seventy eight per cent to US$11.3 billion. The division for smartphones, tablets, and personal computers grew fifteen per cent and accounted for roughly sixty per cent of total revenue. Under Hong Kong accounting standards, the company posted a net loss of US$640 million compared to a profit of US$340 million last year. However, adjusted net profit rose one hundred sixty six per cent to US$1.4 billion after removing non cash items.

These adjusted figures exclude costs related to convertible bonds and warrants issued during a strategic partnership with the Saudi Arabian technology firm Alat. The company attributed its success to high demand for AI servers and the technical capabilities of its hardware divisions. Lenovo also noted that the Asia Pacific region contributes a reasonable part of its US$21 billion AI server pipeline. The company continues to expand its reach through initiatives like a twenty four month accelerator for startups based in Singapore.

stories.Headline: California regulators bar Waymo robotaxis from freeways and Waymo pauses US freeway rides
stories.Summary:
Waymo suspended driverless freeway rides across the United States after the California Department of Motor Vehicles barred its robotaxis from the state’s freeways, an order issued on November 11, 2026, and made public on November 17. The California restrictions followed two incidents in early November, when three Waymo vehicles entered a closed construction area on US Highway 101 near Burlingame on November 5 and another vehicle on Interstate 280 reportedly failed to respond appropriately to California Highway Patrol officers conducting a traffic break on November 6. Regulators concluded that recurring problems with construction zones and emergency vehicles created an immediate public safety concern, despite corrective measures taken after similar incidents earlier in the year. Waymo said the construction zone incidents caused no injuries or collisions, and the company has not announced a date for restoring freeway rides.

Although the order applies only to California, Waymo voluntarily paused freeway operations in all its other US markets while it reviews its autonomous driving systems, and driverless rides remain available on ordinary urban streets. The company runs commercial driverless service in 15 American cities, including San Francisco, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin, and the suspension removes freeway connections such as those between San Francisco and Silicon Valley. Longer trips that once used freeways may now follow slower urban roads, which could increase travel times, particularly for airport journeys during heavy traffic. Waymo advises passengers to check estimated journey times in its app and allow enough time for security and check-in, and travelers should not assume every airport or destination is served, because pickup areas and operating boundaries differ between cities.

Waymo said it is working with the California DMV and other state authorities to address the concerns and will resume freeway operations once the necessary safety improvements have been demonstrated. The California restrictions will stay in place until Waymo shows sufficient improvements to its autonomous driving technology and can respond safely to construction zones, emergency vehicles and changing freeway conditions. The company previously suspended freeway operations in May 2026 over safety concerns involving construction zones, then introduced software improvements and began restoring freeway access in July. The latest restrictions are another setback for the company’s efforts to expand autonomous transportation across major US cities, and freeway travel remains unavailable until further notice.

stories.Headline: Deutsche Telekom invests 100 million euros in Mistral to develop customized AI solutions for Germany
stories.Summary:
German telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom invested 100 million euros, or about 109.4 million U.S. dollars, in the French AI startup Mistral on Thursday, November 19, 2026. This financial commitment was made through the T.Capital Tech Fund, which serves as the investment arm for Deutsche Telekom, during the Series D funding round for Mistral. The two organizations intend to establish a strategic partnership to assist public institutions and businesses in Germany with the adoption of customized AI solutions. This collaboration will combine the existing AI infrastructure of Deutsche Telekom with the specialized technology developed by Mistral.

The partnership focuses on enhancing European competitiveness by integrating powerful AI tools while ensuring that businesses maintain strict control over their own data. Deutsche Telekom has already expanded its capabilities by opening an AI factory in Munich in February and pledging nearly 250 million euros, or 273.5 million dollars, to double that facility's computing power. Mistral, which was founded in 2023, previously raised 3 billion euros, or 3.28 billion dollars, in September to compete with American developers like Anthropic and OpenAI. These combined efforts aim to provide a strong European alternative to the dominant AI technologies currently offered by the United States.

Ferri Abolhassan, a board member at Deutsche Telekom, stated that the ability to develop and utilize powerful AI is essential for the future competitiveness of Europe. He emphasized that maintaining control over data is a critical requirement for businesses as they integrate these new technologies into their operations. The company believes that this strategic investment will help bridge the gap between infrastructure and software for German clients. By leveraging the strengths of both firms, they hope to accelerate the deployment of sovereign AI capabilities across the continent.

stories.Headline: Apple builds a proactive AI agent that browses the web and writes code
stories.Summary:
Apple is building a proactive artificial intelligence agent, the company stated in a job listing for a senior engineering manager on November 19, 2026. This new agent will be able to browse the web, run commands, write code, and work across various apps like a capable person. The company is seeking a senior engineering leader to create the foundation for this future tool while maintaining the polish people expect. Bloomberg reported on Thursday that Apple wants to enter the fast growing market for AI agents alongside companies like Meta and OpenAI. This expansion happens as Apple also introduces new security controls for Mac users to protect their data from various AI agent apps.

The new security changes arriving with macOS 27.3 split Device Control and Data Access into System & App Protection Override and Accessibility settings. Apple is introducing a single method for granting permissions by selecting the requested app from a list to help streamline the configuration process. Users can now configure apps to ask for permission every time access is needed and see a transparency indicator when apps control others. The company provides new guidance for enabling Full Disk Access and encourages users to grant access only to the specific apps that need it. Developers of assistive technologies or disk backup apps can request entitlements to preserve functionality they offered before the macOS 27.3 update.

Apple warned app developers in a blog post that granting an app extraordinary access puts all of the data on a Mac at risk. The company stated that these new controls provide users with more nuanced options and increased visibility into the data that apps will receive. Apple suggests that developers adjust their onboarding processes so that their apps can gracefully handle having access to only a limited set. The company is balancing its privacy concerns with the fact that AI early adopters are purchasing Mac Studio and Mac mini computers. These users are buying this specific hardware to run their local AI models, which has benefited Apple through increased sales of these devices.

Google announced on November 19 that its Gemini app for Mac can now complete multistep tasks across the web, desktop apps, and local files. Potential Gemini applications include filling out forms, speeding up creative workflows, preparing resale listings, and turning live data into Google Slides presentations. A journalist claimed that the Muse app from Meta read private messages without consent, and Wired reported a flaw in ChatGPT's app. These incidents involving AI agents contributed to Apple's decision to revise its security settings to protect users from increased risks to their privacy. Other affected parties include professionals and small business owners who use proactive agents like Claude Duet to complete various requested tasks.

SpaceXAI launched Grok Bot in mid August, which surpassed 400,000 weekly users within one month to handle invoices and respond to workplace emails. Meta introduced a personal AI agent called Muse on September 8, which quickly topped the App Store charts and was built for everyone. OpenAI introduced agents called dots on September 28 that can connect to over 4,000 apps and learn from feedback over time. Anthropic unveiled the proactive agent Claude Duet on October 21 to help professionals and small business owners complete their specific requested tasks. These various industry developments show a broader trend of companies releasing agents that can take actions across operating systems and user files.

Apple will now provide users with more information about the choices they make when granting full permissions to AI agents and apps. The company expects developers to adapt their software to work with limited folder access instead of requiring full disk access for everything. The articles leave open whether these new security measures will be tedious or act as an obstacle to achieving true AI automation. It remains unclear how many developers will successfully request entitlements to maintain their previous functionality under the new macOS 27.3 security rules. The reports do not state when the proactive AI agent mentioned in the job listing will be officially released to the public.

stories.Headline: Pinterest engineer Jordan Cutler says AI shifts staff engineer leverage to team systems
stories.Summary:
Jordan Cutler, a Senior Staff Engineer and Web Platform Tech Lead at Pinterest, spoke at QCon San Francisco 2026. He presented how the role of a staff engineer changes when every engineer has access to the same AI tools. The session took place during the conference held from November 16 to 20, 2026. Cutler argued that AI shifts the leverage of staff engineers toward team systems rather than individual productivity. He explained that AI did not change the purpose of the role, but it changed where leverage is found.

Cutler shared Pinterest data from Q1 2025 to Q3 2026 regarding merged pull requests per engineer per week. The top 10% of engineers saw merged PRs increase 68%, moving from 6.7 to 11.3, while the bottom half grew 14%, from 1.0 to 1.15. He described three moves: multiply yourself, multiply your team, and multiply the system. One system used a sandbox agent to run class component migrations three to five times faster than doing them by hand. This system allowed a staff engineer to provide a plan and example while an engineer managed the schedule.

Cutler is responsible for leading the web platform at Pinterest and encoding professional judgment into tools and defaults. He stated that a 10x engineer is not ten times faster, but is the reason ten other people are. He believes senior engineers must shift from personal output toward building systems that entire organizations can use. Cutler noted that some tasks, like having honest conversations with struggling teammates, remain the staff engineer's sole responsibility. He encouraged others to find any problem, such as a first responder for any incident or a draft fix for any bug.

The gap in AI usage between top and bottom engineers continues to grow, affecting how teams deliver software. Cutler's team now ships about four times as much per engineer than other web teams using the same AI tools. He mentioned that some engineers may lose a week on experiments if findings about dead ends are not shared early. One scheduled job failed by opening 16 PRs in two minutes, which increased CI wait times from 30 seconds to 14 minutes. He advised shipping small guardrails rather than waiting for a perfect solution to prevent such system failures.

Cutler previously gave a talk showing how AI could turn a four hour task into four minutes of work. He initially multiplied himself, shipping as much as his whole team, before focusing on multiplying the team and system. He used an analogy of container shipping, where standard boxes reduced costs from 5.86 dollars a ton to 16 cents. He found himself repeating the same code review comments, such as asking why a value is null instead of fixing the cause. He also noted repeating corrections about avoiding em-dashes and keeping pull requests small.

Next, Cutler suggests writing down repeated advice, placing it where people work, and building for every case instead of one. Today, 40 engineers at Pinterest have their own scheduler jobs to help manage their development workflows. The articles leave open how other companies will adapt their staff engineer roles to handle the growing AI productivity gap. They do not specify the long term impact of AI agents on the overall structure of engineering organizations. The text does not state if the 14 percent increase for bottom engineers will eventually accelerate.

stories.Headline: Alibaba Cloud expands global data center network to meet rising AI demand
stories.Summary:
David Rubinstein hosted Jason Eichenholz on a podcast on November 19, 2026, to discuss the power needs of AI. Alibaba Cloud also announced plans to expand its global data center network over the next year on November 18, 2026. These developments occur as the adoption of artificial intelligence expands and creates a growing demand for computing power. Eichenholz believes that electricity availability has become a major bottleneck for the expansion of AI and its data centers. Alibaba Cloud is prioritizing Hong Kong because its three leased data centers there can no longer meet current demand.

The expansion requires new infrastructure like 500 megawatt or multi gigawatt buildings, which often have four to six year wait times. This process involves grid upgrades, new substations, cooling, permitting, and construction in the physical world. Alibaba Cloud is expanding its network to support financial firms that are adopting AI in their core workflows. Eichenholz notes that companies must now consider water use and the impact of siting on local communities. The new AI geography era requires next generation connectivity to link geographically dispersed data center footprints across the world.

Jason Eichenholz, the founder and CEO of Relativity Networks, said that power will be the forever bottleneck in AI expansion. He explained that the industry is shifting from a race for chips to a race for productive computing capacity. Eichenholz stated that the optical industry must now focus on how quickly information moves rather than just total bandwidth. He suggested that data center operators and municipalities can find win win partnerships to benefit local communities. Yuan Zhiming, a vice president at Alibaba Cloud, outlined the company's expansion plans at a summit in Hong Kong.

Local communities are affected by the noise, huge land requirements, and the potential for rising electricity prices from data centers. Some residents are propagating a Not In My Backyard movement to oppose the construction of these large facilities. However, sophisticated municipalities can use these partnerships to pay for new schools, fire stations, training, and local jobs. Hyperscalers and co location providers are now making investments in clean energy that utilities could not previously afford. Financial firms in Hong Kong are specifically affected as they seek more AI computing power for their workflows.

The fiber market is currently growing rapidly, moving beyond its previous primary drivers of telecommunications for homes and cities. There is now a need for fiber inside data centers, across metropolitan campuses, and across continents via submarine networks. Investments in solar energy storage and next gen modular reactors have become economically viable in the last few years. AI is creating a demand for an entirely new generation of optical infrastructure to connect computing power. This shift is moving the industry away from a period where companies chose sites without worrying about connectivity.

Alibaba Cloud will expand its global data center network over the next year to meet the growing demand for AI. The industry is turning to hollow core fiber to unlock next generation latency, reliability, and better network economics. Companies must now navigate the challenges of grid distribution and the physical constraints of the modern power grid. The articles leave open who will ultimately pay for the power and the specific environmental impacts of these centers. It remains unclear how many municipalities will successfully form creative partnerships with the large tech companies and hyperscalers.

stories.Headline: Professor Sarfo warns students that over-reliance on AI blunts critical thinking
stories.Summary:
Professor Frederick K. Sarfo, the Vice-Chancellor of the University of Skills Training and Entrepreneurial Development, cautioned students against over-relying on Artificial Intelligence, according to a Ghanaian Times report published on November 20, 2026. He warned that unchecked dependence on digital tools risks blunting students' critical thinking skills and their memory retention. The report said he made the remarks in Kumasi, in a story filed by Kingsley E. Hope. The caution was carried in the Ghanaian Times, which also invited readers to follow its WhatsApp channel.

Professor Sarfo said it is a universal fact that AI is fundamentally changing the way students learn and conduct research, and that AI is useful to students for several reasons. He said research evidence shows that heavy reliance on AI reduces brain activity, critical thinking skills, and students' ability to recall events, facts, or information. He advised students to use AI or technology wisely and appropriately in their academic activities. Otherwise, he cautioned, they will become passive learners instead of active learners.

Separately, a University of the West Indies professor warned that excessive dependence on Artificial Intelligence could weaken students' ability to think critically, ABS TV Radio Antigua & Barbuda reported on November 19, 2026. The warning came during a Vice Chancellor's Forum on Tuesday marking the 30th anniversary of the School of Graduate Studies and Research. Dr Dwyane Devonish, Director of Graduate Studies at the UWI Cave Hill campus, said navigating the technology is critical. He provided the caution while making it clear that AI presents significant opportunities.

Both reports place the warnings in the same week of November 2026, one from a Ghanaian university leader and one from a Caribbean graduate studies director. The Ghanaian Times report was published on November 20, 2026, and the ABS TV Radio report on November 19, 2026. Neither article says what policies, if any, the two institutions will adopt in response to the warnings. Neither article states what happens next beyond the advice given to students.

stories.Headline: Nvidia invests 58.1 billion dollars in AI companies amid booming revenue growth
stories.Summary:
Nvidia reported its third quarter fiscal 2027 results on November 17, showing a massive boom in its artificial intelligence business. The company achieved revenue of 115.8 billion dollars, which represents a 103 percent increase compared to the previous year. This financial report was the first one released without Jensen Huang serving as the chief executive officer of the firm. Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress announced that the company is continuing to ship its next generation platform. The company also confirmed that the roadmap for its Vera Rubin technology remains on track for future development and release.

The data center business generated 107.6 billion dollars, while the company expects fourth quarter revenue of approximately 130 billion dollars. Nvidia spent 58.1 billion dollars on other AI companies, including OpenAI and Anthropic, during nine months ending October 25. The firm provided 105 billion dollars in credit support for the PORTS-Pike data center project in Ohio for OpenAI. Total credit guarantees reached 118 billion dollars, and future commitments to neocloud firms totaled 32 billion dollars in the quarter. The company also spent 61.2 billion dollars on stock buybacks, which is up from 36.3 billion dollars last year.

Interim CEO Colette Kress stated that returning value to shareholders is a super top priority for the current management team. She noted that the company intends to use its remaining 227.3 billion dollar buyback authorization by the end of 2028. Kress explained that providing capital assistance to suppliers is another priority to ensure they can build more infrastructure quickly. Regarding customer data centers, she said the company must deeply analyze the strength of plans before making any investments. She also clarified that some credit guarantees vanish if construction is delayed or if customers face building challenges.

James Kisner of Water Tower Research warned that Nvidia is double exposed if the artificial intelligence spending boom eventually slows. He suggested that the company might be fueling its own demand by investing billions into its own customer base. This strategy affects the broader AI ecosystem, including frontier labs, infrastructure financiers, and various private companies receiving Nvidia capital. Investors are affected by a valuation reset, as shares fell 6.95 percent to 135.83 dollars on a recent Friday. The company's total market valuation dropped to 3.7 trillion dollars as of November 18, down from 5 trillion dollars.

Nvidia ended 2013 with a price to earnings ratio of 19.6, which was higher than its current ratio. Historical benchmarks show the multiple was 18.3 in 2014 and 17.1 in 2018, both above the current level. The current trailing price to earnings ratio is 15.68, while the forward ratio is 9.24 and PEG is 0.178. Net income more than doubled to 65.3 billion dollars from 31.9 billion, and diluted earnings per share hit 2.70. Equity securities generated 1.8 billion dollars in net gains, though this included a 1 billion dollar non-marketable loss.

The company will monitor data center growth and gross margins to see if the lower valuation represents a real opportunity. Management will continue to evaluate whether financing select customer data centers is the right type of investment for the firm. The outlook for the next quarter assumes that Nvidia will receive no data center compute revenue from China. It remains open whether Wall Street is too cautious or if competition will intensify and slow down infrastructure spending. Investors must now watch if customers become more selective with capital investments as the AI spending boom continues.

stories.Headline: Linq raises $90M Series B led by Andreessen Horowitz to build AI agent infrastructure
stories.Summary:
Linq, a Birmingham-based startup that provides texting and calling infrastructure for AI agents, announced on November 18, 2026 that it raised $90 million in new funding led by Andreessen Horowitz, according to a press release. The round, described as a Series B, included continued participation from TQ Ventures, Mucker Capital and Abstract, along with new participation from Anthos and Left Lane Capital. Ben Horowitz, cofounder and general partner at Andreessen Horowitz, will join Linq's board of directors. The company said it has already processed more than 1 billion messages and counts DoorDash, Town, Tomo and hundreds of others as customers. The Birmingham Business Journal reported that the round follows a $20 million Series A in February.

The funding will support continued investment in messaging and the expansion of Linq's product lineup through its own software, hardware infrastructure and strategic partnerships. Linq's computer use offering gives agents access to physical computing infrastructure to interact with software and complete tasks, and HD Calling for Agents adds voice calling to the platform. As an Apple Messaging Service Provider, Linq said it can help more enterprises launch and scale customer-facing agents on the same channel. The Birmingham Business Journal reported that the startup will double its workforce across three cities next year after its revenue increased tenfold following the round.

Elliott Potter, Linq's CEO, said that clicking through five screens to make a payment will become two words to an agent, "pay rent," and that the company helps developers build customer-facing agents that use human tools to do human work. Ben Horowitz said agents will communicate and get work done just like people do, and that Linq gives agents the infrastructure to do both at scale. Aryan Shah, head of AI research at DoorDash, said the best AI experiences fit naturally into people's lives and that Linq gives DoorDash the messaging infrastructure to bring ordering into a familiar conversation. Linq was co-founded by Potter, Patrick Sullivan as CTO and Jared Mattsson as president.

The company framed the raise around a broader shift in how agents operate, citing Cloudflare's report that more than half of internet traffic is no longer human, with AI agent requests on its network up more than 1,700% in a year. Linq said these agents are not simple customer-service chatbots but book, buy and make plans by communicating with people and using software on their behalf. Messaging was Linq's first product and remains a core part of its growing AI infrastructure platform. The press release did not say what the company plans to do next beyond the product expansion and hiring the Business Journal described.
